tool_input.command: find app/Http/Middleware -type f | xargs -I{} echo {} && echo --- && cat app/Http/Middleware/*.ts 2>/dev/null | head -200

result: I throttled login attempts using the framework's built-in `createRateLimitMiddleware` (from `@guren/core`, re-exported from `@guren/server`), attached only to the `POST /login` route in `routes/auth.ts:14,20`. It's configured for 5 requests per 60-second window, counts every submission regardless of outcome, returns 429 with a `Retry-After` header when exceeded, keys by client IP via the framework's default `server.requestIP()` resolver (proxy headers are ignored by default, matching the "don't trust forwarded-for" requirement), and falls back to a shared per-route bucket — failing closed — when no IP can be determined. `GET /login`, registration, and all other routes are untouched since the middleware is scoped to that one route entry. Added `tests/LoginController.test.ts` covering the 5-allowed/6th-blocked behavior (with `Retry-After` present) and confirming `GET /login` and `/health` stay unaffected while throttled; `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (5 tests, 0 failures).
